test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 30 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Lavanya got married 10 years ago. Now her age is 1(1)/(5) times her age at the time of marriage. Her son’s present age is one-tenth of her present age. Find her son’s present age.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Age ratio (Now : Marriage) = 1(1/5) : 1 = 6 : 5

Difference in ratio units = 6 − 5 = 1 unit

Given time difference = 10 years ⇒ 1 unit = 10 years

Lavanya's present age = 6 units = 60 years

Son's age = 1/10 × 60 = 6 years

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Marriage happened 10 years ago. Present age = 6/5 of marriage age. Son's age = 1/10 of present age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/617d8e5e96534c7135b98e70d290edecf2d0cf8654e6d9bda87b7154cd614103.png] 

Let marriage age be **x** years.

⇒ Present age = x + 10

⇒ x + 10 = (6/5) × x

⇒ 5(x + 10) = 6x

⇒ 5x + 50 = 6x

⇒ x = 50 years (Age at marriage)

⇒ Lavanya's present age = 50 + 10 = 60 years

⇒ Son's present age = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 years

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Method for Age

If the ratio of ages is given at two different times, the difference between the ratio parts must correspond to the actual years passed.

Age Difference Property

The numerical difference between the ages of two persons remains constant throughout their lives, regardless of the years passed.</p
